title: Asterium Therapeutics - Implementation Launchpad Huddle
header: Date: 2026-02-21 | Start: 10:30 PT | Duration: 58m\nAttendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood Support) -- Dr. Priya Singh, Alan Cortez, Mei Lin, Jason O'Neill (Asterium)
summary: Kickoff-style implementation huddle to align on pilot goals, on-prem VPC/on-prem constraints for PHI workloads, HSM/KMS requirements, observability and canary rollout plan. Agreed pilot scope: two inference routes (clinical notes summarization + triage reranking), staging benchmarks, and security artifacts handoff.
topics: Private deployment options (VPC vs on-prem appliance)
Rollout plan: canary -> gradual traffic -> full prod
Benchmarks: latency SLOs and cost targets
action_items: Jordan Blake: Share onboarding runbook + staging checklist (by 2026-02-24)
Maya Chen: Prepare baseline perf benchmark template and sample traffic replay (by 2026-02-27)
Alan Cortez: Confirm network access matrix and any air-gap constraints; send VPC peering diagram (by 2026-02-25)
Mei Lin: Compile list of compliance artifacts requested (SOC2 scoping, KMS/HSM attestation) and preferred retention window (by 2026-02-26)
Ethan Park: Open initial support ticket for HSM integration with placeholder config and attach logs format sample (by 2026-02-23)
next_steps: Redwood to send deploy runbook + security packet (including SOC2 summary, audit log spec, KMS integration notes)
Customer to grant staging VPC access and a service account with limited perms for pilot
Schedule deep-dive with infra team on 2026-02-27 to walk network and HSM details
Set pilot start for first traffic replay window on 2026-03-02
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Morning everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the CSM on the account, we've got Maya and Ethan with me. Uh quick roll call please.
[00:12] Dr. Singh: Priya here.
[00:15] Alan: Alan, hi.
[00:17] Mei: Mei, thanks.
[00:20] Jason: Jason on product.
[00:22] Jordan: Great, thanks. We're aiming, ah, to just align on pilot goals and the launchpad for the implementation. Agenda is quick: scope, security, infra, observability, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:37] Dr. Singh: Yep, that works. We mostly want to make sure the model serving is PHI-safe, right, so encryption at rest and in flight and key ownership. We also need predictable latency for clinical note summaries.
[00:50] Maya: Totally, Priya. Just to confirm — Asterium wants the private deployment (private control plane + on-prem inference) right? The note in the intake said some workloads will be air-gapped.
[01:03] Alan: Correct. Some endpoints will stay in our on-prem environment behind the HSM. We can't route those through public internet.
[01:10] Maya: Understood — we've done a handful of air-gap installs with customers. Our private option can be packaged as VPC-hosted or fully on-prem. For the HSM integration, we support common HSM providers; we also integrate with cloud K-M-S if you prefer key ownership in your tenancy.
[01:30] Mei: Quick clarification — by "cloud K-M-S" you mean we can use our AWS KMS, or we can have our HSM on-prem, right? Last time I heard "KMS" as a cloud-only thing so want to be clear.
[01:40] Jordan: Yes, both patterns supported; Redwood's private can talk to customer-managed KMS or to an on-prem HSM via a proxy. We'll hand over the integration spec.
[01:50] Jason: For success criteria, from product side we want less than 200ms p50 for the short summarize route and under 600ms p95, with throughput for batch jobs of ~250 qps for reranking — that's our target but flexible.
[02:10] Maya: That's helpful, Jason. We'll validate the p50/p95 with the perf template. Also want to flag quantization changes — if you use an aggressively quantized model we'll need to validate quality regressions.
[02:24] Dr. Singh: Right, quality is the top requirement. We can tolerate some latency increases if it meaningfully improves quality on rare clinical edge cases.
[02:33] Alan: On networking — we will give a staging VPC with a bastion, but the on-prem endpoints will be on a segregated network with strict egress rules. We need a traffic plan for the canary.
[02:45] Maya: Okay, so canary will be internal first — small % of traffic inside staging then widen. For air-gapped endpoints, we do a pre-loaded model bundle and orchestration run locally; so the control-plane calls are limited. There might be small differences in KV cache behavior — our auto prefix cache may need special config for on-prem.
[03:06] Dr. Singh: You mentioned KV cache — we call it K V cash in our notes sometimes — can you explain the implications?
[03:12] Maya: Sure — KV cache holds key/value states for autoregressive decoding. In private deployments, persistent KV cache can be optional; if you disable it you may see slightly higher token compute but simpler stateful control.
[03:25] Alan: We also want to pin model versions. We cannot have a rolling model upgrade without sign-off; that's a big operational constraint.
[03:33] Jordan: Totally understood — we'll enable model pinning on routes and provide the rollout APIs for canary and manual promote.
[03:40] Mei: On compliance, we need audit logs with 7 year retention, evidence for key rotation, and SAM-L SSO for user access. Can Redwood export audit logs in a format that fits our SIEM?
[03:54] Ethan: Yes, we can export logs in JSON line format and push to your collection endpoint, or we can store them in your S3 bucket depending on deployment. We'll attach the sample schema.
[04:07] Dr. Singh: And about certs and attestation for HSM, do you provide an attestation doc or is it one of the items we must generate?
[04:15] Maya: Redwood will provide integration notes and necessary endpoints; the actual HSM attestation is typically provided by the HSM vendor. We will make the support ticket for the HSM handshake and supply logs/var templates for their engineers.
[04:27] Jason: Network latency from the model host back to the control plane — any fallback if the control plane is unreachable? We want graceful degradation.
[04:35] Maya: Yes, there are fallbacks: local runtime can operate in disconnected mode if bundle is present. For hosted-control-plane scenarios, requests can be routed to a local compatible model variant. We'll document the failure modes.
[04:50] Dr. Singh: Benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run a baseline with our sample clinical traffic. We will provide a sanitized replay of anonymized transcripts.
[04:59] Jordan: Perfect — Maya will prepare the perf template and a replay harness; we only need a sample of traffic and the staging VPC creds.
[05:09] Maya: I'll put together the template. One note — transcripts with long context windows will change memory/kv behavior; include typical sequence length distribution if you can.
[05:21] Alan: On the topic of observability: token-level cost breakdown is great; we want to see per-route cost, and tracing from request to model. Also alerting if latency spikes above SLO.
[05:34] Ethan: We have per-route dashboards and tracer hooks, and we can send alerts to your pager. Retention windows can be configured; for compliance logs you may want long-term archival in your own store.
[05:47] Dr. Singh: Timeline — We're aiming for pilot (limited production with 2 routes) in 6 weeks, full production after 10-12 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:57] Maya: That seems reasonable. If staging access and replay arrive by the end of next week we can start benchmarks the week after and aim to have a pilot rollout in early March.
[06:09] Jason: Budget question — for the pilot should we go dedicated capacity or hosted? We're leaning towards a dedicated pool for predictable latency.
[06:18] Jordan: For pilot, we recommend Redwood Dedicated reserved for the high-priority clinical route and hosted for low-risk experiments. That hybrid will keep costs down while giving predictable SLO for the critical path.
[06:30] Mei: Any blocker for SAML SSO? We use an IdP and strict SCIM provisioning.
[06:37] Ethan: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. For Private installs we can integrate with your IdP; we'll need metadata endpoints. We'll also validate RBAC mapping.
[06:49] Dr. Singh: Ok, next steps recap?
[06:52] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send runbook and security packet, Maya to send perf template and replay harness, Ethan to open HSM support ticket, customer to send staging VPC details and compliance list. Pilot start target 2026-03-02.
[07:08] Alan: Sounds good.
[07:10] Mei: One more thing — retention policy for logs: we might have eager requests from legal; can we start with 90 day hot storage and then cold archive to our S3 for 7 years?
[07:20] Ethan: Yes, that's the typical pattern; we can rotate to your archive location daily.
[07:25] Dr. Singh: Great, thanks everyone.
[07:27] Jordan: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive on 2026-02-27.
[07:35] Jason: Appreciate it.
[07:37] End of call.
